enumeration_note: One order-block strategy taught; the three entry models (wick/body/midpoint buy limit) share one skeleton and stop-loss rule, differing only in entry placement and R:R â€” enumerated as one strategy with three variants. Bearish order blocks are mentioned only as the symmetric mirror, never taught as a separate runnable setup. Exit is taught only as an R:R profile (no explicit target level).

coaching_notes: Choosing the right entry model depends on market conditions, the quality of the order block, and your personal risk tolerance
The stronger and cleaner the order block, the more aggressive the entry model you can justify
In weaker or more volatile environments, conservative entries offer greater protection and consistency
Most traders who believe they understand order blocks are actually losing money using them
Order blocks are not random candles or magical zones; they only work when they align with structure, liquidity, imbalance, and mitigation logic
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: bullish market context confirmed by price breaking above the previous major high (valid break of structure) before the OB setup applies
OB identification: bullish order block = last bearish candle before a strong upward displacement that breaks structure
Validation 1 (liquidity sweep): final bearish candle breaks the previous candle's low and immediately reverses upward
Validation 2 (imbalance/FVG): impulsive reversal leaves a fair value gap (non-overlapping candles) above the OB
Validation 2 exception: if no imbalance forms above the sweep candle, extend the OB boundaries to include the next candle where the imbalance forms
Validation 3 (unmitigated): price has not yet returned to retest/trade through the zone
Invalidation rule: if the wick of a candle drops into the potential OB zone during formation, the OB is mitigated â†’ classify invalid and do not trade
Entry trigger: price retraces into the OB and fills resting orders; a change of character (break of an internal low) acts as the entry trigger, not a reversal signal
Entry variant A: buy limit at upper wick of OB candle
Entry variant B: buy limit at upper body of OB candle
Entry variant C: buy limit at midpoint of OB zone
Stop loss: just below the lower wick of the OB candle, adjusted by the spread (all variants)
strategies.entry_summary: In a bullish structure (confirmed break of structure), identify a valid bullish order block â€” the last bearish candle before a displacement that breaks structure â€” validated by three conditions: (1) a liquidity sweep (final bearish candle breaks the previous candle's low then reverses up), (2) imbalance/fair value gap above (if not above the sweep candle, extend the OB to include the next candle where the FVG forms), and (3) the zone remains unmitigated. When price retraces back into the order block (often signaled by a change of character breaking an internal low), enter long with a buy limit order placed at the wick, body, or midpoint of the OB depending on variant.
strategies.exit_summary: Stop loss placed just below the lower wick of the order block candle, adjusted by the spread. Take profit given only as a risk-to-reward profile (aggressive wick entries yield the best R:R, midpoint entries a lower R:R) â€” no explicit target level is taught.
